notes: claude 2.1.251's folder-trust dialog, recorded live and then ANSWERED. PRECONDITION: the dialog only paints in a directory claude has never trusted, so this was recorded in a freshly `git init`-ed /tmp/trustrepo-236 (the `git init` matters — a bare temp dir is a different screen) with `make rebake-corpus HARNESS=claude SCENARIO=trust-dialog WORKDIR=/tmp/trustrepo-236`. The recorder's default workdir is $(CURDIR)/internal/screenbench, inside the repo claude already trusts, where this screen never appears; --workdir exists for exactly this. Re-baking needs a NEW never-trusted directory, because recording once writes trust for that path into the config dir's .claude.json and the dialog will not paint there again. WHAT IT PINS: the dialog is an UNNUMBERED selector — no digits to press — and the default highlight is "No, exit", NOT the trusting row. Confirming it with a bare Enter quits claude at startup, which is the bug this recording exists for; the script answers with Down+Enter as ONE PTY write (\u001b[B\u001b[13u), because an "ESC [ B" split across two writes parses as a lone Esc and cancels the dialog. REPLAY: 2.1.251 runs its TUI on the alternate screen, and both the answered dialog and the recorder's SIGTERM teardown blank the emulator, so a whole-file scr.Write yields a frame with no dialog on it. Replay incrementally and take the FIRST frame carrying the anchor with both option rows — the last one is the post-Down repaint, whose highlight has already moved. pkg/chat/trust_dialog_corpus_test.go does this. Two artifacts only (bytes.raw, meta.json) and no expected.txt: like settled-after-turn this is a screen-shape recording with no ground-truth assistant reply to assert, and screenbench-record only prompts for expected.txt in interactive mode. The trailing reply turn in the script is there to capture the dialog CLEARING, which it does — the composer and footer paint on the alt screen right after the answer. In this bake the reply itself came back "Not logged in · Please run /login": the machine's claude session was expired at record time. That does not affect anything asserted here, all of which is on the pre-answer dialog frame.
